intro_html: Do not skip past this one because of the word pumpkin. Canned pumpkin does not make chili taste like pie. It makes it thick, a little sweet in the background, and velvety in a way that usually takes an hour of reducing. Add a spoon of cocoa powder and a pinch of cinnamon, the same move behind a good mole, and you get a chili with more depth than the standard chili powder and beans version. Nobody guesses the pumpkin. Everybody asks what is in it.
cost_closing_html: About $4.35 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a chili that tastes like it took a lot more effort than it did. Canned pumpkin is one of the cheapest thickeners on the shelf and it brings fiber along with it.
shop_smart: Buy plain canned pumpkin, not pie filling. The pie filling is already sugared and spiced and it costs more. You want the one with a single ingredient on the label.
Cocoa powder is a savory ingredient too. A container lasts years and a spoonful of it is what separates a good chili from a flat one. Same idea as a mole.
Stock up on canned pumpkin in November. It is the one month of the year the price bottoms out, and the cans are good for a very long time.
Frozen chopped spinach disappears into chili. It costs less than fresh, it will not go bad on you, and nobody eating it will notice it is in there.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside covered.
Brown the ground turkey in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up until it is cooked through.
Add the diced onion and chopped green bell peppers and cook until soft, then stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the chili powder, cocoa powder, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, cayenne, salt and black pepper and toast them against the hot pan for a minute.
Add the canned pumpkin puree, the tomato paste, the diced tomatoes with their juice and the chicken broth, and stir until the pumpkin is fully blended into the base.
Add the drained cannellini beans, simmer 30 minutes, then stir in the thawed chopped spinach at the end. Keep the sour cream and cilantro for topping at reheat.
portion_html: Spread the cooked rice into your 14 containers, then set the chili pot on your scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight over the rice. Every serving lands near 563 calories with 33 grams of protein once the sour cream and cilantro go on top.

head.description: Ground turkey chili thickened with canned pumpkin and deepened with cocoa and cinnamon, over rice. A 14 serving batch built for cheap meal prep.
head.keywords: turkey pumpkin chili, pumpkin chili recipe, ground turkey chili, budget meal prep, healthy chili recipe, cheap dinner ideas
steps: Cook the rice separately and set it aside.
Brown the ground turkey, then soften the onion, bell peppers and garlic.
Toast the chili powder, cocoa, cinnamon and cumin in the pot.
Stir in the pumpkin puree, tomato paste, diced tomatoes and broth until smooth.
Add the beans, simmer 30 minutes, finish with spinach, and top with sour cream and cilantro.
